name: Toast
business_model: Cloud restaurant platform combining POS, front- and back-of-house software subscriptions with embedded payment processing (financial technology solutions).
overview: Toast provides a cloud platform for restaurants covering POS, operations and payments. In Q2 2026 it reported about 180,000 locations (up 22%), $2.4B ARR and $60.7B quarterly gross payment volume. Its Advanced Analytics Platform team runs Kafka/Pulsar streaming, Spark and a lakehouse migrating to Apache Iceberg, plus a new Feature Store, over DynamoDB and Postgres operational stores. Toast IQ, an LLM-backed assistant that answers questions over a restaurant's sales, labor and menu data, is a growth product.

sources.title: Toast IQ AI Assistant Overview
sources.excerpt: Toast IQ answers plain-language questions on sales, menu, labor, tips, delivery, marketing and benchmarking by pulling account data and sending it to a third-party enterprise LLM instance, then can make changes after confirmation.

verified_facts.fact: Toast had approximately 180,000 locations as of Q2 2026, up 22% year over year.
Toast ARR was $2.4B as of June 30, 2026, up 25% year over year; Q2 2026 GPV was $60.7B.
Toast's AAP team stack includes AWS, Iceberg, Kafka, Pulsar, Spark, DynamoDB and Postgres.
Toast is migrating from legacy ETL to an Iceberg lakehouse and standing up a Feature Store.
Toast IQ pulls a restaurant's account data and sends it to a dedicated third-party LLM instance to answer questions.
Toast launched the ToastIQ intelligence engine on 2025-05-01.

inferences.inference: Toast IQ's question answering over sales and labor data likely issues many per-tenant analytical queries, making latency and concurrency of the serving layer important.
Building a Feature Store implies a need for an online low-latency store; which technology is chosen is not public.
Running both Kafka and Pulsar suggests historical or team-level divergence in streaming tools, a possible consolidation topic.

opportunity_hypothesis: Hypothesis to validate: Toast is mid-migration (legacy ETL to Iceberg, new Feature Store, scaling streaming) while its LLM-backed Toast IQ assistant needs fast per-restaurant analytics across ~180K locations. SingleStore could fit as the real-time serving tier for Toast IQ and online feature serving, complementing the Iceberg lakehouse. Fit depends on whether current serving layers are a bottleneck, which is not public.

outreach.subject: Serving layer for Toast IQ and the new Feature Store
outreach.body: Hi - I saw your team is moving Toast to an Iceberg lakehouse, standing up a Feature Store and scaling Kafka/Pulsar streaming, while Toast IQ is now answering operators' questions over their own sales and labor data. I'm curious how you think about the serving layer between the lakehouse and those low-latency, per-restaurant queries. SingleStore runs real-time ingest, high-concurrency analytics and vector plus full-text search in one SQL engine, and some teams use it next to Iceberg for online serving. Would a 20-minute conversation to compare approaches be useful?
